corpus_stability.reason: The Oklahoma Driver Manual is a periodically revised official edition, so Section Ten sharing rules change at most with new editions.

items.why: Pedestrian, bicycle, motorcycle, truck, train, and slow-vehicle rules are recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

sections.heading: C — Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Defensive drivers adapt to every road user, pedestrians span walkers, skateboarders, skaters, and wheelchair, walker, and tricycle users, crosswalk walkers beat most vehicles marked or not, crossings channel foot traffic to fixed spots, and machine operators play it safe for jaywalkers in danger [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Stay alert where foot traffic runs heavy, yield blind cane and dog users, guard school zones and playing children, yield sidewalk users at driveways and alleys, never honk, rev, or rush crossers even when entitled, shield hidden crossers behind your stopped car with stop hands and brake taps, and slow for mysteriously halted neighbors who may hide a walker [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists hold equal road rights and duties while usually sharing lanes, swerve without warning for trash, slicks, potholes, dogs, parked cars, and opening doors, and earn at least three passing feet until fully cleared under Title forty-seven-eleven-twelve-oh-eight-A [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A02
Watch unsignaled bike turns especially from children, keep three-foot passing room, never squeeze between a rider and oncoming two-lane traffic but slow and swing left after traffic clears, refuse narrow-street passes, treat residential blocks as danger zones under full vehicle law, mind driveway and parked-car emergence, warn unknowing riders with brief not blasting horns, spot dim night riders despite required front lights and rear reflectors, and merge with bike traffic before right turns instead of cutting across [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A03
Riders hug the shareable right edge yet may command full lanes while overtaking, staging left turns, dodging parked cars, machinery, obstacles, walkers, animals, potholes, and debris, or facing unshareable narrow lanes, flagged hearing-impaired riders earn slowing, and every rider holds the correct traffic lane [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A03
Cyclists slow for stop signs, halt when danger threatens, yield walkers and traffic, and roll through only when safe, while red lights demand full stops with yielding to immediate-hazard traffic before careful passage plus slow-yield right turns on red and stopped-yield lefts onto one-way streets [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A04
Two-thirds of car-motorcycle crashes come from drivers turning across unseen bikes, since motorists scan for cars, narrow short profiles defeat sight and distance judgment, and riders constantly shift position, so motorcycles own full lane width against potholes, blinders, and windblasts, lane sharing is forbidden, and every operator needs an M endorsement [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A04
Pass bikes like cars without close fast air blasts, signal left turns while watching oncoming riders, trail three seconds for emergency room, blind-spot-check every lane change against alongside riders, and expect position shifts for sight, blind-spot escapes, hazard dodges, lane defense, signaling, windblast escapes, exit routes, and turn setups [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A04
Intersections demand waiting out fully clear rider intentions with extra rain, wet, ice, and wind care for impaired bike braking, nights demand dimmed lights against single-lamp misjudgment, awareness hunts narrow profiles everywhere, and statutes require windshields or ANSI goggles and shields against flying objects [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A05
Trucks haul freight with seventy-two percent of goods by road, and followers keep clear sightlines, ride outside blind zones spanning both cab flanks plus two hundred rear feet and ten to twenty hidden front feet under the mirror rule, stop uphill leftward with rollback gaps, dim night lights, and hang back from rain spray [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A05
Truck passes need clear legal zones with headlight-blink announcements, respect weight-driven downhill surges and uphill lags with quick completions and no lingering, never pass-then-slow on downgrades, read return blinks as clearance confirmed by mirror-visible truck fronts, aid passing trucks by holding far and easing speed without accelerating, meet oncoming rigs far right against sideswipes since turbulence pushes apart, and trust twin trailers as safe as singles [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A06
Wide right-turning trucks strand lethal curb gaps that drivers must never enter or pass through, and backing trucks block roads briefly while forbidding any crossing behind inside the blind zone [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A06
Trains never share but always own priority since fifty-five-mile-per-hour consists need a mile or more to halt with every collision the driver fault, half the crashes strike guarded crossings and two-thirds in daylight, impatient beaters gamble thirty-second to two-minute waits, and negligent crossers skip looking, listening, and stopping mostly within twenty-five miles of home [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A07
The law orders halting fifty feet out but no nearer than fifteen from rails and waiting for safety whenever signal devices warn, gates fall or flagmen wave, trains near fifteen hundred feet with audible hazardous approach, or oncoming consists loom plainly close [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A07
Crossing hardware spans early advance signs, R-X-R paint with stay-behind stop lines, yield-like crossbucks with track-count plates, flashing lights demanding full stops until dark with every track cleared, gates demanding halts from first flash until raised and dark, and stop signs demanding complete halts with two-way looks [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A08
Never trap yourself on rails but enter only on certain safe passage and keep rolling once started, never circle lowered gates, caught crossers keep moving since far gates will not pen them, always suspect second trains on multi-track crossings, stalled cars evacuate at once with only twenty seconds from first flash, escapees run forty-five degrees trackside toward the train then dial nine-one-one, and lightless stalls add the blue-white ENS crossing number with exact location and a tracks-blocked warning while racing stays forever forbidden [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A08
Expect hazmat trucks plus school, church, and passenger buses to halt at crossings and prepare to stop behind them, never pass cars or bikes at crossings where tires snag rails, never trust size-shrunk speed and distance judgments by day or night, and always halt and wait on any seen or heard train [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A09
Rural roads hide huge lane-spanning tractors, combines, and farm rigs generally under twenty-five, cresting sixty-five onto them courts disaster, animal-drawn vehicles share equal rights and rules while crumpling easily under posted warning signs, and SMV emblems mark sub-twenty-five farm, construction, and maintenance crawlers [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0058]
